text:
A man known as the “Lip King” who carried out a “Brazilian butt lift” (BBL) on a woman who later died injected her with seven times the amount of filler that he had been taught to use, an inquest jury has been told.
Traces of the filler that Jordan Parke injected into Alice Webb, 33, were discovered in her heart, lungs, brain and kidneys, the inquest heard.
Police told the court in Gloucester they were confident they had a case against Parke for gross negligence manslaughter before he died earlier this year.
They said they had found many more who had “suffered negative experiences” and he had been banned from practising in two areas of the UK because of concerns about his safety record.
Webb, a beautician from Wotton-under-Edge, Gloucestershire, became unwell during the cosmetic procedure carried out by Parke at a beauty salon attached to a house in Gloucester in September 2024. She was taken to Gloucestershire Royal Hospital, where she died in the early hours of the next day.
Webb’s sister-in-law, Morgan Townsend, sobbed as she told the court Webb paid £2,300 for the BBL treatment.
She said Webb sent her a photo of the procedure being carried out and she was “shocked” at how much filler was being used – 1,400ml and “loads” of local anaesthetic. Webb sent a message saying “OMG – it kills” and then simply “Painful”.
The jurors were shown a brief video clip of Parke carrying out the procedure on Webb. He was laughing as he injected her and told her: “Well done!”
Paramedic Allanah Kingston, who went to Webb’s aid when she collapsed, said she was surprised that Parke seemed “unbothered” by what had happened and “didn’t appear to understand the urgency”.
Kingston said Parke did not have personal details about Webb, such as her date of birth or emergency contact information. She added: “I found it strange [he] didn’t come to the hospital.”
Home Office forensic pathologist Dr Stephen Leadbetter said the gel-like filler – hyaluronic acid – was identified in Webb’s lungs, brain, heart, kidneys and thyroid gland. Leadbetter said it could have got into her system when a blood vessel was damaged during the BBL.
DI Adam Stacey, who led the investigation, said there was no formal training for BBLs in the UK but techniques were passed from practitioner to practitioner.
He said Parke had no medical qualifications, but a doctor who had worked with him had recommended using 100ml of filler in each buttock.
Stacey said Parke had been banned from performing BBLs in two areas– Salford in Greater Manchester and Dudley, West Midlands, because of concerns that his methods were not safe, but he was able to carry on elsewhere. “It’s an unregulated industry,” Stacey told the court.
He said: “We were confident we had a case of gross negligence manslaughter.” Officers were about to go back to Parke to ask him more questions about what happened when he died earlier this year. Stacey said Parke’s cause of death was not yet known.
Asked if they had found other clients who had become unwell, Stacey replied: “There were many who suffered negative experiences.”
The inquest continues.
digest_he:
במסגרת חקירת מותה של אלי ווב בת ה-33, נמסר לחבר מושבעים בבריטניה כי ג'ורדן פארק, הידוע בכינוי מלך השפתיים, הזרם לה כמות חומר מילוי הגדולה פי שבעה מהכמות שהוכשר להשתמש בה במהלך הליך הרמת ישבן ברזילאי. עקבות של חומרי המילוי נמצאו בלבה, בריאותיה, במוחה ובכליותיה של המטופלת.

הקורבן חשה רע במהלך ההליך הקוסמטי שבוצע במסבאה מקומית בספטמבר 2024, ומתה זמן קצר לאחר מכן בבית החולים. המשטרה ציינה כי לפארק לא היו הכשרות רפואיות מתאימות, וכי הוא כבר הושעה מביצוע הליכים דומים במספר אזורים עקב חששות לבטיחות מטופליו. המשטרה הייתה בטוחה שיש בידיה תיק מוצק נגד פארק בגין הריגה ברשלנות רבתי, אך הוא מת מוקדם יותר השנה טרם מיצוי ההליכים.
